name: Chemicals, paints and coatings

problems.words: Same shade from two batches looks different and the dealer returns the whole lot
quick_ideas: Write the batch number on every dispatch note from now on — lets you trace a returned can
Keep a retained sample of each batch — gives you something to compare a complaint against.

workzap_build.text: a batch register linking every batch's date, shade and QC result to the dealers it went to, filled right from dispatch.

problems.ask_first: Are complaints mostly on dealer-tinted shades or factory-made shades?
problems.free_stops: The batch-record fields and how complaints are matched are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare returned shade complaints by batch side by side once this week, so you spot whether differences cluster around certain runs.
Make one person sign off the sample kept beside each batch note, so complaints have a clear internal handover point.

problems.words: I can't trace which batch went to which dealer when a complaint comes
quick_ideas: Note batch ranges on each gate pass — links trucks to batches
Ask for a photo of the batch code before discussing any claim — stops claims on stock that isn't yours.

workzap_build.text: a complaint-to-batch tracer where a can's code shows every dealer that batch reached, across all territories.

problems.ask_first: Is the batch number printed on every pack size, including quarters?
problems.free_stops: How codes are captured at dispatch is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many dispatch notes this week show both dealer town and batch, so you see how often traceability breaks.
Give dispatch one register for every outgoing batch and dealer town, so complaint tracing starts from one place.

problems.words: Dealers owe me a lot and some are six months overdue
quick_ideas: List every dealer's balance by age once — shows who to chase first
Set a rough credit limit per dealer — gives your SOs a line not to cross.

workzap_build.text: a dealer ledger with limits, ageing and WhatsApp reminders sent to dealers, flagging orders from dealers over their limit.

problems.ask_first: Who approves dealer credit today, you or the sales officers?
problems.free_stops: Limit rules and the blocking and approval flow are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many overdue balances sit with each dealer town once, so collection visits target the places holding back your cash longest.
Keep one overdue notebook at the sales desk and give one staff member the daily follow up mark, so dealer chasing stays orderly.

problems.words: Schemes are being misused — dealers claim volume they didn't buy
quick_ideas: Check this month's claims against your own invoices before paying — catches inflated volumes
Share each scheme's rules in writing with all dealers — removes "I was told differently".

workzap_build.text: a scheme register that checks every claim against actual purchases before it reaches you for approval.

problems.ask_first: How many schemes are running at the same time right now?
problems.free_stops: The eligibility rules and approval chain are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare claimed scheme volumes with invoiced volumes for the same dealers once, so overstated claims stand out before payout.
Give one person one written list of active scheme claims to review, so approvals stop moving between desks.

problems.words: Painter coupons are being redeemed twice or faked
quick_ideas: Keep one list of redeemed coupon numbers and check it before payouts — stops double redemption
Accept only original coupons — cuts out copies.

workzap_build.text: unique painter coupon codes redeemable once by WhatsApp, recording role and town only.

problems.ask_first: Are coupons redeemed at dealers or at your office?
problems.free_stops: The code rules and redemption checks are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many redeemed coupons arrive with marks or numbers already seen, so you gauge whether repeat claims are isolated or routine.
Give one cashier one notebook for redeemed coupon numbers, so every payout is checked against the same record.

problems.words: Resin price jumped with the dollar and I can't pass it on quickly
quick_ideas: Recost your top SKUs at today's raw-material rates — shows where the squeeze is worst
Talk to your accountant or bank about planning imports around currency swings — that's their area.

workzap_build.text: a cost-per-litre view updated from current raw-material rates and batch yields, flagging products below your target margin.

problems.ask_first: Which raw materials are imported and which are local?
problems.free_stops: The costing model and price-review triggers are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare your latest resin buying note with current selling rates for your busiest paint lines, so you spot where margin pressure is sharpest.
Give one person the job of rewriting the live price list after each resin purchase, so sales quotes catch cost jumps sooner.

problems.words: Pigment consignment stuck at port, production stopped
quick_ideas: Work out how many days of production each imported input covers — shows which one could stop you next
Line up one backup supplier for your most critical input — gives you a fallback.

workzap_build.text: a raw-material board showing stock cover and open consignments, alerting the owner when cover drops low.

problems.ask_first: Which raw material has stopped production most often?
problems.free_stops: Cover levels and the consignment stages tracked are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which stopped production lines depend on the delayed pigment today, so you see the admin impact across orders and planning.
Give one person the port follow up note and evening update, so production hears one version of expected arrival.

problems.words: Sales officers report visits but I don't know if they actually went
quick_ideas: Review each SO's visits against orders received once this week — shows where visits don't turn into orders
Call a few dealers yourself about the last visit — a quick, open check.

workzap_build.text: Sales officers would log visits on their phones with time, location and orders taken, and you would get a daily summary, used openly with the team.

problems.ask_first: How many sales officers are in the field?
problems.free_stops: The visit format and manager reports are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each sales officer's reported visits with orders from those towns once this week, so weak coverage stands out by area.
Give one manager the evening visit summary from every sales officer, so route follow up happens at the same time daily.

problems.words: Dealer orders come on WhatsApp, calls and through SOs — some get missed
quick_ideas: Make one number the only order line — everything lands in one place
Confirm every order back to the dealer — catches misses the same day.

workzap_build.text: one order book for WhatsApp, calls and SO orders, tracked to dispatch with confirmations sent to buyers.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many dealer orders come in a day?
problems.free_stops: The order intake flow and status messages are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count orders from calls, sales officers and messages that were booked late this week, so you see where misses happen most.
Give one staff member one order notebook for every incoming channel, so booking no longer depends on scattered handovers.

problems.words: Factory supervisor and accounts each keep their own numbers
quick_ideas: Pick the three numbers you want daily — keeps everyone focused
Settle yesterday's mismatches in one short morning meeting — stops gaps growing.

workzap_build.text: a morning read of sales by territory, receivables, raw-material cover and open complaints from one source.

problems.ask_first: Which numbers disagree most between the two?
problems.free_stops: Which figures feed the daily read and from where is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which daily numbers factory supervisor and accounts both write this week, so you see where duplicate effort and mismatches start.
Give one clerk one notebook for the agreed daily numbers, so factory and accounts read from the same page.

never_say: No formulation, recipe, VOC, hazard classification, storage or dangerous-goods transport advice.
Never say a product meets or fails PSQCA, ESMA/UAE or Canadian standards.
Never help mislabel, re-date expired stock, copy another brand's packaging or under-invoice imports; decline.
Spills, fires, fumes or burns: stop and point to emergency services.
No advice on effluent or environmental rules; note admin effort only.
Never store dealers' or painters' names or numbers; roles and towns only.

sample_reply.person: Can you suggest a solution? Dealers keep sending back full cartons over shade complaints and we never know which batch they're from.
sample_reply.pi:
Sure, this is fixable, and the first steps are simple.
First, write the batch number on every dispatch note, so any returned carton can be traced.
Second, keep a retained sample of each batch to compare complaints against.
To make it last, Workzap could put in place: a batch register that links each batch to the dealers it went to, so one code shows where else it was sent.

Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're free to say no.
